Rashi on Pesachim 60a:10:1.hebrew: לעולם בשתי עבודות - ודקשיא לך, פשיטא, הא איפסיל ליה מעבודה קמייתא:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:10:1.english: Actually, [it is] about two rites - And [as for] what was difficult for you, "It is obvious, for it was disqualified from the first rite!"

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:10:2.hebrew: איידי דתנא לשמו ושלא לשמו - לאשמעינן דמחשבין מעבודה לעבודה כדלעיל, תנא נמי שלא לשמו ולשמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:10:2.english: Since [the Mishnah] taught "for its own sake and not for its own sake" - to teach us that one can have [disqualifying] intent from one service to another, as above, it also taught "not for its own sake and for its own sake."

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:1.hebrew: שלא לאוכליו - לחולה ולזקן שאין יכולין לאכול כזית, ואין בו מנויין אחרים אלא הן:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:1.english: For those who cannot eat it - For a sick person or an elderly person who cannot eat an olive-bulk, and there are no other registered [people] for it except them.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:2.hebrew: פסול - דאיש לפי אכלו כתיב (שמות י״ב:ד׳), הראוי לאכול:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:2.english: It is disqualified - For it is written, "every man according to his eating" (Exodus 12:4), [meaning one] who is fit to eat.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:3.hebrew: שלא למנוייו - נימנו עליו חבורה זו, ושחטה לשם חבורה אחרת:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:3.english: Not for those registered for it - This group registered for it, and he slaughtered it for the sake of another group.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:4.hebrew: לערלים - ישראל שמתו אחיו מחמת מילה, והן פסולין מלאכול פסח, דכתיב "כל ערל לא יאכל בו" (שם):
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:4.english: For uncircumcised [people] - A Jew whose brothers died as a result of circumcision, and they are disqualified from eating the Paschal lamb, as it is written: "No uncircumcised person shall eat of it" (ibid.).

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:5.english: Ritually impure [people] - [They are] also forbidden from [partaking of] consecrated foods, and they are [liable] to karet for eating them.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:6.english: Here it is obvious [that] it refers to one rite - For there is [only] one intent.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:7.hebrew: רישא נמי בעבודה אחת - כלומר, אפילו בעבודה אחת, ודלא כר' מאיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:11:7.english: The first clause [is] also about one rite - That is to say, even about one rite, and not in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:12:1.english: Are [the two cases] comparable - Is this indeed a proof?

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:12:2.hebrew: סיפא - דבמחשבה אחת מיירי, ליכא לאוקומה אלא בעבודה אחת:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:12:2.english: The latter clause - Since it speaks of one intention, it cannot be established except [as referring] to one rite.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:12:3.hebrew: רישא - דמיירי בשתי מחשבות, איכא לאוקומא אי אף בעבודה אחת, ודלא כר' מאיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:12:3.english: The first clause - Which deals with two [different] intentions, can be established either [as referring] even to one rite, and not in accordance with Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:12:4.hebrew: אי בשתי עבודות - ולא בעבודה אחת, ור' מאיר:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:12:4.english: Or about two services - and not about one service, and [it is according to] Rabbi Meir.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:13:1.english: For those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it - As [the Gemara] goes on to explain.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:13:2.hebrew: היכי דמי אי נימא בשתי עבודות - שחטו לאוכליו ע"מ לזרוק שלא לאוכליו, ואשמעי' דכשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:13:2.english: What are the circumstances? If we say during two rites - [That] he slaughtered it for those who can eat it in order to sprinkle [its blood] for those who cannot eat it, and [the mishna] teaches us that it is valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:13:3.hebrew: וטעמא מאי משום דאין מחשבת אוכלין - אין מחשבת פסול האוכלין, כגון חולה וזקן, פוסלת בזריקה; דבשחיטה הוא דכתיבי אוכלין, "לפי אכלו תכוסו", והיינו תשחוט, כדמתרגמי' "ושחט" — "ויכוס":
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:13:3.english: And what is the reason? Because there is no intent concerning eaters - Disqualifying intent regarding the eaters, such as a sick or elderly person [who cannot eat], does not invalidate [the offering] during the sprinkling [of the blood], for it is with respect to slaughter that eaters are written [in Scripture]: "According to his eating you shall count [tachosu]," and that means "you shall slaughter," as we translate [the Hebrew] veshachat ["and he shall slaughter"] as veyichos.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:14:1.hebrew: ה"ג בעבודה אחת, כגון בשחיטה דמהני' בה מחשבת אוכלין, פסול - ואפי' כה"ג דאמר לאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:14:1.english: This is the reading: During one rite, such as the slaughter, during which intent with regard to those who will eat is effective, [it is] disqualified - And even in such a case, where he said, "For those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it."

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:14:3.hebrew: מקצת אוכלין - כגון הכא דנימנו בו ראויין לאכול ושחטו לשם כולן, כשר, דהא כולה שחיטה נמי משום אוכלין צריכה, דאי אפשר לכזית בשר בלא שחיטה. ולקמן מפרש מאי שנא דלשמו ושלא לשמו פסול, ולאוכליו ושלא לאוכליו כשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:14:3.english: Some of those who are to eat - For example, here, where [people] fit to eat were registered on it and he slaughtered it for the sake of all of them, [it is] valid, for the entire slaughter as well is needed for [the sake of] those who eat, since it is impossible [to obtain] an olive-bulk of meat without slaughter. And later [the Gemara] explains what the difference is, that [slaughtering] for its own sake and not for its own sake [is] disqualified, whereas [slaughtering] for those who can eat it and for those who cannot eat it [is] valid.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:1:1.hebrew: או דילמא בשתי עבודות תנן - אחת חישב לשמו ובשניה שלא לשמו. והכא ליכא למימר תפוס לשון ראשון, שהרי ארבעתן העבודות חשובות זו כזו ליפסול את הזבח באחת מהן, ואפילו לרבי מאיר מיפסיל:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:1:1.english: Or perhaps we learned [it regarding] two rites - [During] one he intended [it] for its own sake, and during the second not for its own sake. And here one cannot say "hold [to] the first expression," for all four of them — the [blood] rites — are [equally] significant, one like the other, to disqualify the offering through [any] one of them, and even according to Rabbi Meir it is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:1:2.hebrew: ומהדר גמרא, אהייא מהני לישני דסיפא דמתניתין קיימא הך בעיא:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:1:2.english: And the Gemara asks: Regarding which of these formulations of the latter clause of the Mishnah does this dilemma apply?

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:2:1.hebrew: אי נימא אשלא לשמו - ברישא והדר לשמו, הא בין לר' מאיר בין לר' יוסי אפילו בעבודה אחת מיפסיל. לר' מאיר — דהא אמר תפוס לשון ראשון; לרבי יוסי נמי מיפסיל — דהא ר' יוסי אף בגמר אית ליה, כלומר: תחלת דבריו של אדם וסופן, בכולן דעתו נתפסת וכולן מתקיימין:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:2:1.english: If we say [that it refers to] not for its own sake - first, and then for its own sake, behold, both according to Rabbi Meir and according to Rabbi Yosei, even during a single rite it is disqualified. According to Rabbi Meir, for he said, "Hold by the first expression"; according to Rabbi Yosei too it is disqualified, for Rabbi Yosei holds "even at the conclusion [of his words]," meaning that [both] the beginning of a person's words and their end — in all of them his intention takes effect and all of them are upheld.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:2:2.hebrew: אלשמו ושלא לשמו - דאי בעבודה אחת נמי פסיל ליה, מתני' תו לא מיתוקמא כרבי מאיר, דאמר תפוס לשון ראשון ולשון אחרון לא חייל:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:2:2.english: Concerning "for its own purpose and not for its own purpose" - For if [the Tanna] disqualifies it even during one rite, the Mishnah can no longer be established according to Rabbi Meir, who says: Hold fast to the first statement, and the last statement does not take effect.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:3:1.hebrew: אי נימא כדקתני - שחט וקיבל והלך וזרק כולן שלא לשמו, ולאו "או" קאמר — למה לי בכולהו? הא בחדא קי"ל בזבחי' בשמעתא קמייתא דהזבח נפסל:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:3:1.english: If we say as it teaches - [That] he slaughtered, and received, and carried, and sprinkled all of them not for its own sake, and it does not mean "or" — why do I need [improper intention] in all of them? Behold, with [even] one [of them] we hold in Zevachim, in the first sugya, that the sacrifice is disqualified.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:6:1.hebrew: לעולם - סיפא נמי דקתני לשמו ושלא לשמו, בשתי עבודות. ודקשיא לך היינו רישא — לא תיקשי: רישא מיירי דכי שחט חישב בה לשמו, וכשזרק חישב בה שלא לשמו; וסיפא מיירי דבשעת שחיטה חישב תרתי מחשבות — חדא על השחיטה לשמו, וחדא על הזריקה שלא לשמו:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:6:1.english: Actually - the latter clause too, which teaches 'for its own sake and not for its own sake,' [is referring to] two rites. And as for what was difficult for you, [namely that] this is [identical to] the first clause — let it not be difficult: the first clause deals with [a case] where when he slaughtered, he intended regarding it for its own sake, and when he sprinkled [the blood], he intended regarding it not for its own sake; whereas the latter clause deals with [a case] where at the time of slaughtering he thought two thoughts — one regarding the slaughtering for its own sake, and one regarding the sprinkling not for its own sake.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:7:1.hebrew: דאמר הריני שוחט לשמו - על מנת לזרוק שלא לשמו. והכא ליכא למימר "תפוס לשון ראשון", דהא אעבודה אחריתי קאי לשון שני. וקא משמע לן מתני' דמחשבין מעבודה לעבודה, כלומר: דמחשב בשעת עבודה זו על חברתה לעשותה במחשבת פסול — נפסל מיד, ואפילו לא עשה השניה במחשבת פסול, כמו שחיטה:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:7:1.english: [Where] he said: "I am hereby slaughtering [it] for its own sake" - in order to sprinkle [its blood] not for its own sake. And here one cannot say, "Hold by the first statement," because the second statement refers to a different rite. And the Mishnah teaches us that one can intend from one rite to another rite — that is to say, when one intends during this rite regarding its fellow [rite] to perform it with a disqualifying intent, [the offering] is disqualified immediately, even if he did not perform the second [rite] with a disqualifying intent, just like [improper intent regarding] slaughtering.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:7:2.hebrew: והיינו בעיא דרב פפא - דאמר מחשבים מעבודה לעבודה, בשחיטת קדשים בפ"ק (ד' י), דאמרינן התם, מתקיף לה רב פפא, דילמא הא קמ"ל דמחשבין מעבודה לעבודה:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:7:2.english: And this was the question of Rav Pappa - who said [that] one can intend from one rite to another rite, in Shechitat Kodashim [Zevachim], in the first chapter (fol. 10), where it is stated there: Rav Pappa objects to it, "Perhaps this is what it teaches us, that one can intend from one rite to another rite."

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:8:1.hebrew: השתא לשמו ושלא לשמו - דעבודה ראשונה בכשרות, אמרת פסול במחשבת עבודה שניה:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:8:1.english: Now, for its own sake and not for its own sake - where the first service [was performed] validly, you say [it is] disqualified by the intent of the second service.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:8:2.hebrew: שלא לשמו ולשמו מיבעיא - דכיון דנפסל בעבודה ראשונה, מהיכן יחזור ויוכשר:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:8:2.english: Not for its own purpose and for its own purpose — is it necessary [to state]? - For since it was disqualified in the first rite, how could it become fit again?

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:9:1.hebrew: אלא לאו בעבודה אחת - ותנא לשמו ושלא לשמו, לאפוקי מדרבי מאיר דאמר תפוס לשון ראשון. ותנא שלא לשמו ולשמו, דלא תימא תפוס לשון אחרון, דהא הדר ביה מקמא וכי שחיט אהאי בתרא קא שחיט; קמ"ל דר' יוסי הוא, דאמר בכל דבריו אדם נתפס, ולא הדר ביה, אלא אתרוייהו איכוין:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:9:1.english: Rather, isn't [it] during one rite - And [the Tanna] taught "for its own sake and not for its own sake" to exclude [the view of] Rabbi Meir, who says: "Hold by the first expression." And [the Tanna] taught "not for its own sake and for its own sake" so that you should not say: "Hold by the last expression, for he retracted from the first [intention], and when he slaughters, it is with this latter [intention] that he slaughters." [Therefore, the Mishnah] teaches us that it is [the view of] Rabbi Yosei, who says: "A person is held [liable] for all his words," and he did not retract, rather he had both [intentions] in mind.

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:9:2.hebrew: ומדסיפא - שלא לשמו ולשמו בעבודה אחת קאמר, דבשתי עבודות לא איצטריך:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:9:2.english: And since the latter clause - [The clause] "not for its own sake and for its own sake" is speaking of one service, for regarding two services it would not be necessary [to state it].

Rashi on Pesachim 60a:9:3.hebrew: רישא - דלשמו ושלא לשמו נמי אף בעבודה אחת, ור' יוסי היא:
Rashi on Pesachim 60a:9:3.english: The first clause - [which deals with] "for its own sake and not for its own sake" [is] also even in a single rite, and it is [the view of] Rabbi Yosei.

Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:11:1.hebrew: שחטו שלא לאוכליו - פי' רש"י: לחולה ולזקן, ואין מנויין עליו אלא הן. וקשה: אם כן מאי איריא שלא לאוכליו? אפי' סתם נמי פסול, כיון שאין לו אוכלין. ונראה דמיירי דיש נמי מנויים אחרים:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:11:1.english: If he slaughtered it for those who cannot eat it - Rashi explained: [it refers] to a sick person or an elderly person, and none are registered for it except them. And this is difficult: if so, why [specify] "for those who cannot eat it"? Even [if slaughtered] without specified intent, it is also disqualified, since it has no eaters. Rather, it appears that [the Mishnah] is speaking [of a case] where there are also other registered [participants].

Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:13:1.hebrew: אילימא בב' עבודות, טעמא דחשיב בזריקה - נראה לר"י, דהכא איירי אליבא דרבה, דאמר לקמן (פסחים ד' סא:): שחטו למולין על מנת שיתכפרו בו ערלים — כשר; דלרב חסדא דאמר פסול, לא מצי מיירי בשתי עבודות. מיהו לקמן משמע במסקנא, דאף לרבה פסול:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:13:1.english: "If we say [it refers to] two rites, [is] the reason [that it is valid] because he had intent during the sprinkling?" - It appears to the Ri that here [the Gemara] is speaking according to Rabbah, who says later (Pesachim 61b): [If] one slaughtered it for circumcised people on condition that uncircumcised people should gain atonement through it, it is valid; for according to Rav Chisda, who says it is invalid, [the Gemara] could not be speaking of two rites. However, later in the conclusion [of the sugya] it is implied that even according to Rabbah it is invalid.

Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:2:1.hebrew: אבל בשתי עבודות אפי' ר' מאיר מודה - וא"ת: והיכי מיתוקמא מתני' כר' מאיר? הא קתני סיפא: "לטמאים ולטהורים כשר", ואמאי? נימא "תפוס לשון ראשון", ובעבודה אחת מיירי, דאין מחשבת טמאים אלא בשחיטה. וי"ל: דמתני' מיירי כגון דקיימי קמיה טמאים וטהורים, ואמר "הריני שוחט לאלו"; דבענין אחר לא משכחת מקצת ערלה דלא פסלה לר' מאיר אליבא דרבא, דאמר "אינה לשחיטה אלא לבסוף":
Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:2:1.english: "But in [the case of] two rites, even Rabbi Meir agrees" - And if you ask: How can the Mishnah be established in accordance with Rabbi Meir? Surely the latter clause teaches: "[If he slaughtered it] for impure people and for pure people, it is valid." Why [is it valid]? Let us say, "Follow the first expression," and [moreover] it is speaking of a single rite, since the intention regarding impure people applies only during slaughtering. And one can answer: The Mishnah is speaking of a case where impure and pure people are standing before him, and he said, "Behold, I am slaughtering for these"; for in any other way you do not find [a case of] partial uncircumcision that does not disqualify according to Rabbi Meir, according to Rava, who says: "Slaughtering is only [effective] at the end."

Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:5:1.hebrew: אי בשתי עבודות היינו רישא - וא"ת: ולימא דרישא איירי כששחט סתמא, ולכך כשזרק שלא לשמו אמר "הוכיח סופו על תחלתו", אבל אם אמר בהדיא "הריני שוחט לשמו", ה"א דלא עקר שלא לשמו אפי' בשתי עבודות — להכי איצטריך סיפא? וי"ל: דסברא הוא, דבשתי עבודות אינו מועיל מפרש יותר מסתם:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:5:1.english: "If [we say] during two rites, that is the first clause" - And if you ask: Let [the Gemara] say that the first clause refers to where he slaughtered without specifying [any intention], and therefore when he threw [the blood] for a different purpose, [the Tanna] said [that] "its end proves its beginning"; however, if he explicitly said, "I am slaughtering for its own purpose," I would have thought that [an intention] for a different purpose does not uproot [the initial intention] even during two rites — for this [reason], the latter clause is necessary? And one can answer: It is a matter of logic that during two rites, specifying explicitly is no more effective than [slaughtering] without specifying.

Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:7:1.hebrew: והיינו בעיא דרב פפא - פי' הקונט' דחוק, דנקט רב פפא ולא נקט ר' יוחנן, דאמר התם בהדיא: "מחשבין מעבודה לעבודה". ונראה לריב"א דגר' לעיל: "בעי רב פפא: בעבודה אחת תנן", ומסיק: "היינו בעיא דרב פפא"; פי': שפיר מתוקמא בעיא דרב פפא, שאינו יכול לפושט' מן המשנה, וכן מצא רבי בספר ישן, וכן גר"ח. ורשב"א מפרש: "והיינו בעיא דרב פפא" — מה ששאל: "בעבודה אחת תנן או בשתי עבודות?", הנך שתי עבודו' היינו כגון שוחט לשמו על מנת לזרוק שלא לשמו:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:7:1.english: And this is the inquiry of Rav Pappa - Rashi's explanation is forced, for [why did the Gemara] mention Rav Pappa and not mention R. Yochanan, who explicitly stated there [in Zevachim]: "One can intend from one rite to another rite"? Rather, it appears to Riva that we read earlier [in the Gemara]: "Rav Pappa inquired: Did we learn [this in the Mishnah] regarding a single rite?" And [the Gemara here] concludes: "This is the inquiry of Rav Pappa"; meaning: Rav Pappa's inquiry is well-established, as he cannot resolve it from the Mishnah. And so my teacher found in an old book, and so Rabbenu Chananel read. And Rashba explains: "And this is the inquiry of Rav Pappa" — regarding what he asked: "Did we learn [this] regarding a single rite or regarding two rites?" — those two rites are, for example, one who slaughters [the offering] for its own purpose on condition to sprinkle [its blood] for a different purpose.

Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:8:1.hebrew: שלא לשמו ולשמו מיבעיא - וא"ת: כי נמי אמרי' בעבודה אחת, תיקשי ליה הכי: השתא לשמו ושלא לשמו פסול, שלא לשמו ולשמו מבעיא? דאפי' ר' מאיר דפליג בלשמו ושלא לשמו, בשלא לשמו ולשמו מודה, דלכ"ע תפוס לשון ראשון! וי"ל דאי בעבודה אחת מיירי, קא משמע לן — כמו שפירש בקונ' — דלא אזלינן בתר לשון אחרון [דוקא], לאפוקי מבן ננס דאית ליה בפרק בית כור (בבא בתרא ד' קה.): תפוס לשון אחרון לגמרי לבטל הראשון. ור"י מפרש דבעבודה אחת אתי שפיר דתני "שלא לשמו ולשמו" אגב "לשמו ושלא לשמו", כיון דשניהם בעבודה אחת; אבל בשתי עבודות — דרישא הפסול בזריקה וסיפא הפסול בשחיטה — לא דמו אהדדי, ולית ליה למתניי' אגב רישא:
Tosafot on Pesachim 60a:8:1.english: "For a different purpose and for its own purpose, is it necessary [to say]?" - And if you say: Even if we say [it is speaking] about one rite, it should still be difficult for it thus: Now [that] "for its own purpose and for a different purpose" is disqualified, is it necessary [to say] "for a different purpose and for its own purpose"? For even Rabbi Meir, who disagrees regarding "for its own purpose and for a different purpose," concedes regarding "for a different purpose and for its own purpose," since according to everyone, [one] follows the first expression! And one can answer that if it is speaking about one rite, it teaches us — as [Rashi] explained in the Kuntres — that we do not follow [specifically] the latter expression, to exclude [the view of] Ben Nannas, who holds in the chapter [entitled] Bayit Kor (Bava Batra 105a) [that one] follows the latter expression completely to nullify the first. And R"I explains that regarding one rite, it works out well that [the Mishnah] teaches "for a different purpose and for its own purpose" alongside "for its own purpose and for a different purpose," since both of them are in one rite; however, regarding two rites — where in the first clause the disqualification is in the sprinkling, and in the latter clause the disqualification is in the slaughtering — they are not similar to one another, and [the Tanna] would not teach it alongside the first clause.
